reasoning: The model wrongly treats generic-subject conditional/sufficiency claims (which are just A→B style declaratives, per Step 3's own mapping) as implicit universal generalizations. The skill needs an explicit clarification that sentences matching the 'X is necessary/sufficient for Y', 'if A then B' patterns are conditionals to be translated per Step 3, not excluded as FOL, since Step 3 already provides direct translation rules for them — excluding them creates an internal contradiction.

edits.target: - An implicit universal generalization even without "all"/"every" (e.g. "Students who study pass" = "all students who study pass").
edits.content: - An implicit universal generalization even without "all"/"every" (e.g. "Students who study pass" = "all students who study pass") — this applies only when the sentence generalizes over a class of individuals/entities. It does NOT apply to conditional-style claims relating two abstract states of affairs (e.g. "A passing grade is sufficient for graduation eligibility", "if it rains, the ground is wet") — these are plain propositional conditionals per Step 3's sufficient/necessary/if-then mappings, not first-order generalizations, even though no specific individual is named.
